answers.readable_answer: Roll separately for each office card, adding 1 for each fatigue on that card and another 1 for the Chairman. A result of 1–2 does nothing; 3–4 adds fatigue; 5 or more retires the member. Move the retiring member to Pensioners, flip the card into Vacant Offices, and return its fatigue to the supply.

Each player who retires at least one pensioner must take or discard one card from the display. Players act in descending order of actual total retirement spending, with ties broken by most total windows and then clockwise order from the Prime Minister. Players may peek at blackmail cards in the display. Stop selections when the display is empty. Discard any remaining display cards and refill it with three cards, with blackmail facedown and prestige faceup, even if nobody took a card. Return unretired pensioners to the supply.

Take the selected normal action once, or twice if the opportunity marker was already there at the start of the phase, and move the marker to the main action. Only the latest passed extra-action law may be used. Its extra action receives no marker doubling and does not move the marker. Four or more vacant offices allow one extra writer once per turn, so repeating Enlist Writer can place three writers in total.

For Seek Share, pay the printed price of an empty Stock Exchange space to the bank. At the end of the Family phase, while Debt and applicants both remain, move the rightmost applicant into the Court and reduce Debt by one for each share created. Once there is no Debt, move remaining applicants as far right as possible while preserving their order. The purchase money does not enter a Company treasury.

Fill vacancies in ascending order of the office numbers on the card backs. Insert any vacancy created by promotion into that same order. Hiring your own family member requires verbal consent from every other player represented in the candidate pool, except in a Chairman election. Move a promoted member's fatigue to the new card. If there is no candidate, or the hiring office is vacant, skip the office: it remains vacant and takes no actions, including hiring.

A Chairman candidate must own a Company share and obtain the consent of players controlling a pure majority, meaning more than half, of the current shares. The first candidate to obtain that support is elected. If the election deadlocks, the former Chairman chooses any shareholder, including themself, without Nepotism consent. The winner moves one share into the Chairman slot. It remains a share but cannot be traded or used for firm investment.

Commit money from the office treasury and the required resources, gather the dice, and then subtract the penalty. Read the lowest die: 1–2 succeeds; 3–4 fails and permits a retry if sufficient resources remain; 5–6 is catastrophic. On catastrophe, the office takes no further actions, the officeholder returns to the supply, the card is flipped into Vacant Offices, and fatigue returns to the supply, subject to specific office exceptions. An action must have an effect or a chance of success.

The Chairman may advance Debt three times freely, adding £5 to Company Balance each time. Every further advance requires consent from the majority of shareholders, counting the Chairman share, and Debt cannot pass the end of its track. The Chairman must allocate all Company Balance to other office treasuries and reduce Balance accordingly. Borrowing may be interleaved with allocation while respecting the limit.

Shipping must spend until at most £2 remains. Leasing an extra ship costs £2, fitting a ship from a shipyard costs £3 and requires no owner consent, and buying a Company ship costs £5 and is allowed only when no ships remain on shipyards. Place acquired ships in any sea zone; China becomes eligible once created. Return extra ships at Refresh.

Declare the home region and only other regions that are actually reachable through an open route with sufficient ships. Spend £1 per die, then subtract one die per declared nonhome region. On success, fill as many orders as possible in the declared regions, up to one per ship. Start at the home port, then place adjacent to your own previously placed writers. Use filled-order tokens if writers run out. Another Presidency's home region cannot be filled, even if its office is vacant. The Company receives the printed order values, the President receives £1 per filled order, and each writer's owner receives £1 per writer placed. Each President may have at most one successful Trade per turn.

Deploy may target the Presidency's home region, an associated region, or a region bordering an associated region. It cannot target another home region or another Presidency's Company-controlled region. A Company-controlled target must have a closed order or unrest. Exhaust active officers and regiments for one die each, and use alliances for their printed strength. Subtract the target's strength and the full strength of its empire; a Company-controlled defender has strength zero. After every attempt, roll once per exhausted officer: each 6 removes an officer to its owner's supply. Regiments are never removed by this check.

Loot is £4 per tower plus the faceup loot modifier, with a minimum equal to the number of surviving officers used plus 1. Pay the Commander £1 plus £1 for each of their surviving officers used, then pay other officers clockwise, then pay the bank £1 per regiment or alliance piece. Repeat until the loot is gone. The Commander gains one trophy per tower. Remove the tower and dome; if it was a capital, remove the matching flags. Clear unrest and open all orders. For a newly conquered region, put its loot token region-side up above the President, place its Governor overlay, put its Governor card in the vacant stack, and establish Company control. Redirect the Elephant inward if it was there facing outward. On catastrophe, lose half the trophies, rounded up, and return the Commander to the supply; still check losses for exhausted officers.

Begin with the printed dice pool. Roll that pool without a penalty and remove one die after every attempt. Success gives a £1 bonus, plus another £1 if the preceding roll failed. Choose to build a Company ship in two successful stages, add a regiment to the associated Army, or add an unsplit £2 to Company Balance or the President's treasury. Each Tax after the first in the turn adds unrest, and every unsuccessful check adds unrest. Attempts may continue until the Governor stops, the pool is exhausted, or catastrophe occurs, applying the general vacancy rule.

Expenses are £1 per current Debt, per officer or regiment excluding the Commander, and per ship in sea zones, including China. Each emergency loan adds £5. Advance Debt if possible, but continue borrowing even at maximum Debt. New Debt adds no interest this turn, and Balance then becomes zero. One or two emergency loans lower Standing by one; three or more lower it by two. Next compare Balance with expectations at the current Standing and lower Standing by one if Balance is below expectations. Then optional dividends pay £1 per share, including the Chairman share. A total dividend payout strictly greater than expectations advances Standing once. Reaching the failure space causes immediate Company failure.

Resolve the primary attack first, then attacks on all other Company regions with unrest, in Bombay, Madras, and Bengal Army order. Each Commander chooses the order within their own regions. The primary attack uses normal Invasion or Rebellion strength plus local unrest; secondary attacks use only unrest. Exhaust newly active Army strength equal to the attack, or as much as possible. Insufficient defense causes Region Loss. A successful defense clears unrest and gives the Commander a trophy. For a vacant Commander, Military Affairs acts instead, followed by the Chairman if necessary; the acting substitute gains or loses no trophies.

Support of −1 or lower means the law fails. Discard it and resolve any dilemma's If Failed text. The Opposition Leader returns the marker and becomes Prime Minister, then moves the selected policy one adjacent space in either direction and resolves it. Support of zero or higher passes the law: place it with passed laws, give the Prime Minister a token, resolve the selected policy's consequence, and then apply the law's immediate effects. Restore vote cards. If legislation causes Company failure, finish the vote before Final Scoring.

In 1758 and Long 1710, the Prime Minister may call Deregulation at the start of the turn before London Season if Standing or Debt is on a lined space, and must call it if either is on a starred space. On passage, reduce Debt by one for every two Debt, set Standing to S, give the Prime Minister a law token, and activate deregulation. On failure, raise the share VP value up to ±3, keep the law, and retain the Prime Minister. There is no policy, and the Prime Minister may vote against Deregulation.

A player who is not a firm manager may form a firm by returning an eligible Company share or flipping a workshop to its invested side. Flip the player's board, create a family firm share, set value to the leftmost space, and take £5 from the bank into London. Later investment requires the manager's consent; the same share or workshop payment adds £5 to London and creates a new share. Company shares cannot be used when Standing or Debt is on a lined space. A share created this turn cannot be used, even after it has been traded, and the Chairman piece is unavailable. Invested workshops give neither a bonus nor Company-failure VP. The ten-share cap does not prevent further investments, which create no new shares.

After investments, managers secretly choose a home port and sea zone and commit a London cash bid. A firm needs a ship, but may select a closed home port. Reveal the cash while keeping the strategy secret. At the start of the associated Presidency's operations, reveal the strategy and make one check using bid dice, paying the bid to the bank. Successful initiative is the number of ships minus the number of dice showing 1 or 2; a successful President's Trade uses the same calculation. Fill orders from lowest initiative upward, with the President deciding ties. If the President is absent or does not trade, wait until the Commander and Governors have had their opportunities, and let the Chairman decide ties. Each firm fills at most ships plus one open, connected orders from the chosen home port, once each. Orders already filled by others may be filled for half their listed value, rounded down. Revenue goes to India; advance firm value one space per £6 of revenue this turn.

At the start of Revenue, firms act in initiative order, followed by other firms. Break ties by the manager's windows, then clockwise from the Prime Minister. Expenses are £1 per ship plus the higher of the share count or firm value, paid from either treasury. A firm that cannot pay dissolves unless rescued: shares go to Debtors' Prison at −1 VP each, ships return to shipyards, the charter returns to its family side, and workshops remain invested. Dividends come only from India and pay £1 per share plus £1 to the manager for each dividend. A shareholder may forgo payment with the manager's consent. Record the total paid on the retirement marker, then move the remaining India cash to London.

Cash, trophies, passed-law tokens, dice, and regiments may be represented by proxies. The Balance, VP, and Vote tracks are unlimited. Other supplies are limited; complete as much as possible when they run out. Everything, including discards, is public except facedown blackmail. Firm strategy and bid selection are temporarily secret.

Players may trade enterprises, facedown blackmail, family cash, shares, and promises. They may not trade officeholders, writers, officers, prizes, spouses, passed laws, played blackmail, the Prime Minister dial, trophies, or the Chairman piece. Replace a transferred share with a piece from the recipient's family. Played blackmail is faceup and untradeable; unplayed blackmail may be peeked at but must be traded facedown. Adjust VP when luxury ownership changes.

Immediate transfers are binding, while future deals are nonbinding. A printed promise card may compel its guarantor to act if able and within the card's timing. Promise cards may be traded to third parties or back to the guarantor. They cannot be called during Final Scoring. If simultaneous calls cannot all be fulfilled, the guarantor chooses which to fulfill. Transferring a resource cannot activate it twice, as with a workshop bonus.

At five players, add three extra setup cards; at six players, add six. Shuffle and deal them evenly. Take all printed holdings: put members in their offices and take their cards, put shares in the Court, put writers and officers in their indicated boxes, and place Commanders in their slots without cards. Each shipyard's ship goes in the listed sea zone, or on the shipyard if unfitted. Each starting luxury gives 2 VP. Shuffle prestige and blackmail together and deal a three-card display, with prestige faceup and blackmail facedown. Shuffle the laws.

The game ends on the scenario's final turn or when Standing reaches the leftmost failure space. Failure is ordinarily immediate, but failure during Events allows Events to finish, and failure caused by a law allows the vote to finish. During Final Scoring, negotiation, promises, and blackmail are prohibited unless a card explicitly permits them.

Use the Power track for enterprises, including prestige enterprises, and Company shares; the bottom two positions give zero power. Each passed law and trophy adds 1, the Prime Minister adds 2, and applicable card power counts, including faceup or facedown blackmail and spouses. Award first- and second-place points from the board table for the final turn. If players tie for first, each receives only the lower award and nobody else receives an award. A tie for second gives no points. Break a tie in final VP by most windows, then clockwise order from the Prime Minister.

If the Company survives, add the current Court VP value for each Company share, then perform final office attrition and retire pensioners without prestige. If it fails, subtract that same value per share, add 1 VP per uninvested workshop, and draw a random failure card instead of conducting normal final retirements. Scores may be negative. A firm special retirement is available before these steps regardless of the Company's outcome.

A spouse cannot be transferred and imposes its permanent printed restriction. Negotiate any required trades immediately upon taking the spouse. Discounts are personal and may stack; each can be used once per London Season and once during Final Scoring. Discounts reduce actual spending for prestige priority.

Ships remain fitted and in play when their shipyards are returned. A returned shipyard cannot be purchased while its matching ship is in play. Losing a luxury or prize removes its points when applicable.

Enlist Writer places one writer in a Presidency; the once-per-turn extra writer for vacancies is separate. Enlist Officer places one officer in Training. A luxury costs £4 paid to the bank, is worth 2 VP while owned, and is a social enterprise with a window. A shipyard costs £2 paid to the bank, comes with its matching unfitted ship, is a shipping enterprise, gives one vote, and gives a £1 bonus if fitted. A workshop costs £5 paid to the bank, is a manufacturing enterprise, gives two votes and a £1 bonus, and is worth 1 VP if the Company fails unless invested. Seek Share pays the printed cost of an empty space to the bank and creates an applicant.

Take a member from any of your own prizes and lose its printed VP. This also applies when creating firm shares. If no action is possible, take no action and return the opportunity marker to the supply.
The former Chairman automatically becomes the next Chairman. Place a member from the supply, or use a member from a prize if possible and lose its VP. If neither is possible, there is no Chairman.

The Chairman hires the Director from current officeholders other than themself or Governors, or from writers if all offices are vacant. The Chairman may hire any writer for Shipping or China. Military Affairs is hired from Commanders, or from officers if there are no Commanders, or from Training if there are no officers. The Director hires a President from that Presidency's writers or Governors. A President hires a Governor from associated writers or officers, never a Commander.

Each envoy die costs £1 from the treasury, with no penalty. Repeat envoys while able. Success opens a closed non-Company order or creates China, with the Chairman immediately hiring a writer. Afterward, make up to two transfers, each moving one writer or ship between Presidencies or sea zones, including China.

First make up to two Army transfers of officers or regiments, keeping them in the top half. Then assign all trainees to the top half of Armies. Finally, appoint Commanders when a position is vacant or a family has strictly more Army pieces than the incumbent's family, choosing among the largest families. The previous Commander returns as an officer in the top half. A tie with the incumbent preserves the incumbent, and Nepotism does not apply.

The President orders their own Trade, Commander, and Governors, and must give each an opportunity. Commanders and Governors may decline. Each position completes all actions before the next begins; Trade may occur before or after positions but cannot interrupt them. If the Presidency is vacant, the Chairman chooses the order but cannot trade or approve alliance purchases.

Trade capacity is one order per ship; ships are not exhausted as Army pieces are. Writers placed on routes return to their associated Presidency, rather than an arbitrary writer box or the writer box of the region's home Presidency. Use a divider between adjacent writers from different Presidencies. Remove tokens and dividers at Refresh.

At the start of their own operations, the Commander requests alliances. The President approves and pays the printed cost from their treasury, then the alliances move to the top. Each alliance may be used once during its purchase turn, for Deploy or defense, at its full unsplit strength. Active alliances become exhausted at Refresh, unlike officers and regiments, which reactivate.

A Company-controlled defender has strength zero, and Deploy is allowed only if the region has a closed order or unrest. After the loss check, minimum loot is £1 for each surviving officer used plus £1 for the Commander. A region with zero towers gives zero tower trophies. Open all orders and clear unrest, but do not create a new Governorship.

Building a Company ship requires two successes. The first places the ship in the region, where it has no other effect; the next Build success moves it to the associated Presidency's sea zone. A regiment goes into the associated Army. It has officer-like strength, pays its loot to the bank, and makes no officer-loss rolls.

China is created by an Envoy success or the Envoy to China law, and the Chairman immediately hires any writer. Its treasury holds ships only. Shipping and the Director may assign or move ships there as to a sea zone. China acts after Bengal, and its ships count as Eastern for expenses, events, storms, and laws.

China permits only one attempt, and no attempt is allowed without export icons in Company-controlled regions. Roll one die per ship. On success, add £4 to Balance for each export in all Company regions and pay the Superintendent £1 for each. Do not count exports in non-Company regions.

Move Governors to Pensioners and remove their overlays and partially built ships. No new Governors or Governor overlays are created. Replace the Director's holder and card with the Governor General, preserving fatigue, treasury, and turn position; put Governor and Director cards in the box. The Governor General hires Presidents, is hired like the Director, and undergoes normal attrition. Subsequent region losses skip Governor elimination.

Before checks, add £3 to Balance for each controlled region. Spend £1 from the treasury per die. Every 6 rolled adds unrest to every controlled region, and an unsuccessful check adds one further unrest to each. Success pays the acting player £1 per region and requires one benefit per region: a ship in any sea zone including China, a regiment in any Army, or a £2 Tax into Balance or any treasury except their own. Tax adds unrest; multiple Tax choices must put their unrest in different regions. Govern can succeed at most once; failures may be retried while resources remain and the result is not catastrophic.

Roll for each affected player-owned ship. A 1–2 does nothing; 3–4 adds fatigue, or sinks an already fatigued ship; 5–6 sinks it. A sunk ship returns to its shipyard unfatigued. Company and extra ships are exempt. China is Eastern; firm ships use their strategy's zone, and Hobnob ships are exempt.

Return a writer to the supply when its order closes, or flip a filled token to its closed side. A fully closed source region Cascades to connected orders. If a connected target order is already closed, close the northernmost open order in that region; if none is open, Cascade there. Each region may initiate a Cascade once per tile but may receive multiple effects.

Turmoil closes the northernmost open order in the top-stack region, or Cascades. Windfall pays £1 per writer on orders in the top-stack region and adjacent regions. For Shuffle, March first, shuffle the tile with the remaining draw stack, then shuffle the discards and put them on top. If the draw stack is empty, March last instead.
A sovereign top-stack region gains a tower; a dominated one rebels with the printed explosion modifier. March only when the Elephant was fully inside a Company region that successfully rebelled.

If the Elephant is on a border, open the connected orders across that border and add a tower to each touched non-Company region. If it is fully inside a region, instead open all local orders and remove unrest. Then March.

The attacker's whole empire strength plus the modifier must strictly exceed the defender's whole empire strength. On success, give the defender a dominated flag; taking the defender's capital shatters its old empire. An unflagged attacker creates a capital flag and a small flag if a set is available; otherwise, no flags or new empire are created. On failure, the attacker loses one tower.

Compare only the rebel's strength with that of its sovereign capital, adding the modifier to the attacker. The attacker must be strictly stronger, so a tie fails. On success, remove the rebel's flag and close its open orders, or Cascade if all are already closed. On failure, remove a tower from the capital rather than the rebel.

Return the Commander to the supply and lose half the family's trophies, rounded up. Roll for each officer in the associated Army, returning each officer that rolls a 6 to the supply. Return the Governor card to the unused stack and its member and fatigue to the supply. Remove the overlay, partially built ship, and unrest. Restore a dome with one tower and the appropriate invasion flag. Return the token to the region loot-side down and remove its Presidency association. An Invasion closes orders or Cascades; other attack types have already done so. The first region lost lowers Standing by one, the second by two, and so on. Other regions are not automatically lost: resolve each of their attacks.

After a successful Invasion, use Imperial Ambitions to move to the successful capital; otherwise, use the top-stack region. Place the Elephant fully inside a Company region. In a dominated region, point it toward its sovereign. In a sovereign region, use the shape-marked border toward a neighbor, skipping dominated neighbors clockwise. If all neighbors are dominated, use the redirect-arrow shape's border toward the capital.

Use the storm die to select targets: West means Bombay, South means Madras, and East means Bengal. An all result targets each; a none result uses the top-stack region. Roll a die for each target's strength and resolve an Invasion or Company defense. On success, close orders once, or Cascade if all were already closed; remove the flag, or all matching flags if it was a capital; restore the dome in a Company region; and set strength to half the attack die, rounded down. March using the circle only if the Elephant was fully inside a Company region that was invaded.

Reveal laws one at a time, up to three. A previously drawn law may be selected; discard the others. Drawing a dilemma forces its selection and stops drawing. Choose clockwise or counterclockwise around the dial and stop at the first matching law icon. The policy includes its target and consequence, and the arm moves before the vote. Read the law and set its starting support.

Tax charges £1 per target; return any unpaid target, including the Chairman. Window tax additionally charges for every window on enterprises and prize members; return an enterprise or member if unaffordable. Bonus pays £1 per target. Power swaps the target with the next higher position; if the target is highest, choose any other pair. Prestige enterprises count.

Votes come from family cash at £1 per vote, plus card icons used once per vote by rotating the cards. Voting proceeds clockwise, beginning with the Prime Minister. After a full round, the Prime Minister may call another full round or stop; a round with zero votes must resolve. The support track is unlimited, using counters as needed. Restore used cards after the vote.

A supporter may later oppose, but an opponent cannot support again during that vote. The player with the most opposition votes becomes Opposition Leader; an incumbent retains the position on a tie. With consent, votes may be cast for a player who is already opposing or committed to opposing, and count toward that player's total. The Prime Minister cannot oppose or consent to the use of their enterprises, but a vote promise may force those enterprises to vote against.

Pay upkeep for each prize, even on the final turn. Return an unpaid member to the supply and lose its VP. On the final turn, skip Refresh and proceed to scoring. Otherwise, return writers to their associated Presidency, tokens, dividers, and extra ships to the supply, reactivate officers and regiments, exhaust active alliances, and advance the turn.

Each shareholder may make one special retirement per London Season from the supply; the allowance is per shareholder, not per firm. Cash spent is capped by the highest total dividend marker among firms in which that shareholder owns a share. An absent or zero marker gives no eligibility. Discounts may allow a prize's printed cost to exceed the cap. Otherwise use normal retirement rules, including prestige. At the start of Final Scoring, after scoring firms, allow the retirement regardless of Company success or failure, without prestige.

Investments go to London, while trade revenue goes to India. London pays for ship fitting and bids; either treasury may pay expenses; only India pays dividends. After dividends, move remaining India money to London. Family cash cannot be transferred into or out of firm treasuries.

Investments occur after the Family phase is complete, including new-share creation, and before Hiring. There is no fixed investment order: continue until nobody wants further actions, then choose strategies simultaneously. The firm manager resolves timing conflicts within a firm; the Prime Minister resolves them between firms.

Fitting a ship from a shipyard requires consent and costs £3 paid to the bank. Firms cannot acquire Company or extra ships. With the owner's consent, a firm may buy back a fitted player ship for £3 if unfatigued or £2 if fatigued, paying from London into Shipping's treasury.

The initiator must not already be a firm manager and needs majority shareholder consent, but need not be a shareholder themself. Move the firm's ships, cash, and shares to the initiator's charter, copy the value and dividend cube positions, and reset the former manager's board and cubes.

Every shareholder of all merging firms must consent. The highest-value firm is primary; if tied, players choose. Negotiate share transfers, and return shares above ten only with their owners' consent. The entire immediate agreement is binding. Consolidate all ships, shares, and treasury funds at the primary firm, and return secondary charters to their family sides.
Hobnob has no cash bid, trade, or dividends, but the firm must still pay expenses. Keep its previous dividend marker instead of setting it to zero. Its ships are exempt from storms.

Emergency investments are allowed at the share cap but create no new shares there. Use the same eligible Company-share or workshop procedure with manager consent. Immature Company shares remain unusable, and the weak-share restriction still applies. Pay expenses, lose unused cash, and reduce Value by one space per investment.

A firm facing dissolution may merge with one other firm, with negotiated shareholder consent under the normal rules. The other firm must first pay its own expenses if it has not already done so, as well as the endangered firm's outstanding expenses.

Voluntary dissolution requires every shareholder's consent. Apply the normal dissolution procedure: shares go to Debtors' Prison at −1 VP each, ships return to their matching shipyards, the charter returns to its family side, and workshops remain invested.

At the start of scoring, gain or lose the printed firm VP per share and lose 1 VP per piece in Debtors' Prison. Total fractional VP before rounding down. Then allow one eligible special retirement regardless of Company survival, followed by normal Power and Court scoring and final retirement or failure procedures.

For each family member on a prize, the five entries list cost, upkeep, VP, and windows in this order: £2, zero upkeep, 0 VP, 0 windows; £4, £1 upkeep, 2 VP, 1 window; £8, £2 upkeep, 4 VP, 2 windows; £14, £3 upkeep, 8 VP, 3 windows; and £20, £4 upkeep, 12 VP, 4 windows.

The 1710 scenario runs turns 1–5 under a monopoly without deregulation. The 1758 scenario runs turns 3–7 and may deregulate. The 1813 scenario runs turns 5–8 and starts deregulated. Long 1710 runs turns 1–8 and may deregulate.

In 1710, expectations are £10, Debt is zero, each treasury receives £3, Royal Protection is in effect, each Army has one regiment, and there are no Company ships. In 1758, expectations are £12, Debt is 3, each treasury receives £4, Calico Acts is in effect, each Army has one regiment, there is one Company ship in the East, and Bengal's control token is with the Bengal Presidency.

Expectations are £10, Debt is zero, and each treasury receives £3. Use Military Oversight, Deregulation on its Debtors' Prison side, and Calico Acts. Put two regiments in each Army, one Company ship in each zone, and the +2/−2 share token in the Court. Put the Governor General law in the box; its overlay replaces the Director. Create the China office and place the three home-region control tokens with their matching Presidencies.

The first- and second-place awards are 3 and 1, 5 and 2, and 8 and 4, respectively. In a tie for first, each tied player receives only the lower award—1, 2, or 4, respectively—and nobody else receives an award.

Social enterprises have power 2, Company shares have power 1, and shipping and manufacturing enterprises have power zero. Standing spaces with expectations of £4, £6, and £8 are lined, as are Debt spaces 5–8. The starred Standing space at £4 or Debt space 8 forces the vote. Standing S has expectations of £10.

Neither of the two proposed adjustments applies. The primary attack uses only the ordinary die, and the resulting tower strength is the die result divided by two, rounded down. Normal secondary unrest attacks against the Company still apply. On success, close orders once; Cascade only if they were already closed.

For Connections, zero dice means failure. Fraud occurs at the start of Revenue: reduce Balance by twice the highest officeholder roll, to a minimum of zero, and take that cash from the bank. Impeachment returns the holder to the supply and puts the card in Vacant Offices. A demoted Commander becomes an officer and is eligible for reappointment.

ambiguities.original_wording: subtract target and full empire strength
ambiguities.issue: This wording can count the target twice if full empire strength includes it. The readable answer deliberately preserves the old formulation. The parent identified a later source correction as target plus OTHER empire regions, counted once; that correction has not been applied here.

ambiguities.original_wording: Must take from any own prize
ambiguities.issue: The fixed answer does not state the triggering condition for taking a member from a prize. No supply-exhaustion condition has been added from outside this key.
The fixed answer does not itself state the triggering condition for this fallback. The paraphrase preserves the instruction without supplying an external condition.

ambiguities.original_wording: Successful Invasion capital via Imperial Ambitions
ambiguities.issue: Successful capital is not precisely identified in the compact text. The paraphrase preserves that wording rather than selecting an attacker or defender capital.

ambiguities.original_wording: £1 family per vote plus card icons once per vote
ambiguities.issue: The compact wording does not explicitly distinguish cash-funded votes from icon-funded votes, or whether once per vote means once per entire voting session. The paraphrase retains the key's wording without adding an interpretation.
The compact text does not explicitly say whether the majority is measured by shares or by shareholder headcount. The paraphrase retains majority shareholder consent without selecting a metric.
The key gives five prize-value entries without prize names. The paraphrase preserves their order and values without inventing names.
The referents for respectively are absent from the fixed answer. The paraphrase preserves the three ordered award pairs without adding final-turn or scenario labels.
The two alternatives rejected by Neither are not identified in this key entry. The paraphrase acknowledges two proposed adjustments without naming them.
The compact text does not specify who rolls, who receives the bank cash, or whether that cash equals the uncapped calculation or the actual capped reduction. The paraphrase preserves those gaps.
